title: What to include in a freight broker shipper packet
seoTitle: What to include in a freight broker shipper packet
searchIntent: What should a freight broker send in a shipper onboarding packet?
excerpt: Build a useful shipper packet with accurate capabilities, contacts, relevant credentials and a clear explanation of your carrier qualification process.
takeaway: Make the packet useful to the people approving and using your service. Every capability and credential should be accurate and relevant.

sections.title: Send the packet at a meaningful point in the conversation
paragraphs: Luis positions the shipper packet as support for a developing business relationship. Sending unsolicited attachments does not replace learning who handles transportation or what the shipper needs.

After a relevant conversation, ask what the company requires for vendor review. That lets you provide useful information instead of expecting the recipient to sort through a generic collection of documents.

sections.title: Start with a clear account of your capabilities
paragraphs: Use a concise introduction that explains the freight services you actually provide and how to reach the right people. Keep claims specific enough for the customer to understand the fit.

Do not add modes, geographic coverage, results or references that you cannot support. If a prospective customer needs a specialized service, explain the relevant capability honestly rather than making the packet appear broader than the business.

sections.title: Include the credentials relevant to the relationship
paragraphs: Provide appropriate business and registration information and the financial-security or insurance documents relevant to the customer’s review. Verify that the information is current and belongs to the correct legal entity.

Not every document applies in the same way to every business model. Avoid presenting a long list of credentials as proof that all risks are covered. Answer the customer’s actual requirements and resolve uncertainties with the appropriate professional.

sections.title: Explain the carrier qualification process you use
paragraphs: Luis suggests giving the shipper a concise account of the brokerage’s qualification process. This helps procurement or compliance understand how a carrier is selected beyond the sales conversation.

Describe real controls and responsibilities. A polished two- or three-page explanation is only useful if the team performs the stated checks. Do not promise a verification process that exists only in the packet.

sections.title: Help the internal handoff
paragraphs: The person speaking with you may need to forward the packet to another department. Clear contacts, relevant documentation and a concise capabilities page make that handoff easier.

If you provide references, obtain permission and ensure the contact information is suitable for the intended use. Make it easy for the customer to ask a follow-up question without exposing unnecessary personal or sensitive information.

sections.title: Keep documents current and share them deliberately
paragraphs: Review the packet when contacts, credentials or capabilities change. Use verified channels for sensitive information and confirm the recipient before sending documents that could be misused.
The packet supports trust; it is not a substitute for ongoing performance. Match what it promises with the way you communicate, qualify carriers and manage the customer’s shipments.
